items.headline: OpenAI to retire GPT-4, GPT-3.5 Turbo, o1, o1-pro, o3-mini and o4-mini on 23 October
items.note: Verified on OpenAI's own deprecations page: a mass shutdown of six model families, including GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 Turbo, effective 23 October 2026 — a dated, vendor-forced retirement that any team building on these APIs must migrate off before the deadline.

items.headline: JPMorgan opens Q3 2026 bank earnings season on 13 October, with Citi expected the same week
items.source: Hudson Labs (earnings preview, citing consensus data)
items.note: Consensus for JPMorgan: revenue of $50.85bn, EPS of $5.86, against a tough Q3 2025 comparison ($47.12bn revenue, $5.07 EPS). Preview flags capital-markets normalisation, expense growth versus revenue, and over $40bn of excess capital still to deploy between buybacks, organic growth and M&A — exactly the trigger the queue has been waiting on.

items.headline: Jamie Dimon says hyperscaler AI spending could top $1 trillion next year, adding to inflation before it eases
items.note: At the J.P. Morgan India Conference, Dimon put next year's AI infrastructure spend above $1 trillion, said it could add roughly 1% to GDP growth, and argued it adds to inflation now but should turn disinflationary once the steepest part of the build-out passes — the exact inflation-now/deflation-later tension the essay is framed around.
